title: Quick check: Integrating Non-React Libraries

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Integrating Non-React Libraries”?
options: The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
External widgets should synchronize with an external system and clean up obsolete work when needed.
questions.answer_key: External widgets should synchronize with an external system and clean up obsolete work when needed.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Integrating Non-React Libraries: External widgets should synchronize with an external system and clean up obsolete work when needed.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying External widgets?
options: Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Include reactive dependencies and clean up subscriptions or requests that are no longer current.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
questions.answer_key: Include reactive dependencies and clean up subscriptions or requests that are no longer current.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Integrating Non-React Libraries: Include reactive dependencies and clean up subscriptions or requests that are no longer current.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Integrating Non-React Libraries” complete?
options: Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Integrating Non-React Libraries: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
